newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria to set up $54 mln youth job creation scheme.
newsitem.headline: Algeria to set up $54 mln youth job creation scheme.

text.p: Algeria, moving to a free market economy, is to set up a state youth job creation scheme based on a fund of three billion dinars ($54 million) this year, the prime minister said on Tuesday.
Ahmed Ouyahia said unemployment was a central concern and the new national promotion "must effectively come into action before the end of this year."
"The process of developing public works to generate massive permanent employment must continue...during 1997," he told a cabinet meeting.
Algerian officials have said a lack of jobs and poverty attract young people to the Islamist fundamentalists who have been fighting for five years to topple the government.

Labour Minister Hasene Laskri said authorities in 1996 had focused on saving nearly 400,000 jobs. Diplomats and economists in Algeria have long warned that bloated state and local industry would have to shed jobs to become competitive.
An estimated 1.7 million people work in state industry which, outside the energy sector, largely operates at about 50 percent capacity, according to Algerian officials.
